verdict: constant, and it cost this repository a day
why: Every one of the 20 trials rendered the b/ directory as ARTIFACT A, because detection-draw captures round 1 of a stubbed loop and loop.js alternates sides by (round + critic index) parity. The batch therefore CANNOT distinguish 'the mapping is always b' from 'the mapping alternates'. That is not a harmless constant: the inverted detection rate published on 2026-08-27 survived a full day precisely because no trial in the batch disagreed with any other about the mapping. A batch drawing some trials from round 1 and some from round 2 would have produced two contradictory rates inside one run and exposed the inversion immediately. Any future batch should cross the mapping; this one cannot, and no claim here may rest on the mapping having varied.

verdict: THE INSTANCE ISSUE 50 IS ABOUT, found mechanically
why: true on all 48 rows of the pairing cohort. The comparability probe was correct on every draw of every pairing, so this run could not have produced an incorrect prediction and no claim about the probe's accuracy is falsifiable by it. That is exactly what issue 50 says about docs/runs/2026-08-26-pairing-stability.md: five of six pairings in the false-refusal cell put an unambiguous worker against an unambiguous worker, so the set was chosen for clarity and a wrong answer was not meaningfully available. The write-up asserts the opposite in prose — 'it did not come back against its author, and it could have' — which is why this check reads the ledger instead. The honest bound is: correct on pairings nobody expected to be marginal. Issue 33 exists to build a set whose answers nobody authored.

verdict: constant BY CONSTRUCTION — the hash and the grounding are the same fact
why: Every constructed row whose artifact exists is grounded mechanically: its role is derived by running it (scripts/constructed-verify.mjs), and that is what makes the set ground truth nobody authored. The one row without an artifact_hash is the absence row, whose ground truth is that there is nothing to hash. So the cohort that carries a hash is exactly the cohort that can be executed, and grounding cannot vary inside it. The cohort exists because the hashes were added on 2026-08-30 (issue 33) so oracle-record could pin an observation to the bytes it was made against; it is a pin, not a second experiment. The moment an agentically-grounded row is added to this file the constant breaks and this row stops being consulted.
